newsitem.title: USA: Los Angeles voters go to polls to choose mayor.
newsitem.headline: Los Angeles voters go to polls to choose mayor.

text.p: Voters turned out on Tuesday to choose the next mayor of the second-largest U.S. city, with incumbent Richard Riordan a strong favourite to be elected to a second term in office.
His opponent is former activist Tom Hayden who represents Los Angeles in the California state Senate.
Voter turnout was expected to be low, with officials predicting that only about 30 percent of the electorate would go to the polls.

Riordan, a wealthy businessman who accepts a salary of only $1 a year as mayor and who was first elected in 1993, has run a low-key campaign, admitting that electioneering is not his strong point. Nevertheless, the latest Los Angeles Times poll showed him with a 20-point lead over Hayden and easily capable of garnering the 51 percent of the votes needed for re-election.
If neither candidate gains more than 50 percent, a run-off election will be held in June.

Although Riordan is a Republican and Hayden a Democrat, the race has been non-partisan with neither candidate running under his party banner. Indeed, Riordan has the backing of several prominent local Democrats while there are a number of Republicans in Hayden's camp.

Hayden, who was once married to actress Jane Fonda when both were anti-Vietnam War activists, injected the only real note of acrimony into the campaign when he accused Riordan of being a "racist" -- a remark he quickly withdrew.

Hayden, a former head of the militant Students for a Democratic Society (SDS), who had been part of the famous Chicago Seven trial of war protesters, is expected to garner more black votes than his opponent.

Also on the slate on Tuesday was the race for city attorney between the incumbent, James Hahn, whose father, Kenneth Hahn, was a longtime Los Angeles county supervisor, and San Fernando Valley attorney Ted Stein. The two have spent a total of more than $2.5 million on their campaigns.
Voters were also being asked to vote on an initiative to rewrite the city's 72-year-old charter and another that would raise $2.4 billion to repair and renovate ageing city schools.
